raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
# Description

Six `RuntimeError` messages in the fusible-op API build one string from four fragments and leave the `f` off the first one, so the brace expression that names the offending subclass goes out verbatim:

```
{self.__class__.__name__} operation has 1 extra tensor inputs and 0 extra tensor outputs.
It should override `fuser_forward` instead of `op_forward`.
```

The two fragments after it are f-strings and do interpolate, so the counts are right and only the class name is lost, which is the one part a caller cannot work out for themselves. These are the guards that fire when a subclass declares extra tensor inputs or outputs and implements `op_forward` / `op_backward` instead of `fuser_forward` / `fuser_backward`, so the message exists to say which operation got it wrong.

The same four-fragment message appears six more times in the same tree with the `f` in place, in `basic/swiglu.py:499`, `:507`, `basic/activation.py:383`, `:391`, `basic/grouped_linear.py:852` and `:860`. These six were the ones that were missed.

Demonstrated standalone, since it is a property of the language rather than of TE:

```python
class Demo:
    num_extra_inputs = 1
    num_extra_outputs = 0

    def msg(self):
        return (
            "{self.__class__.__name__} operation has "
            f"{self.num_extra_inputs} extra tensor inputs "
            f"and {self.num_extra_outputs} extra tensor outputs. "
            "It should override `fuser_forward` instead of `op_forward`."
        )


print(Demo().msg())
```

```
{self.__class__.__name__} operation has 1 extra tensor inputs and 0 extra tensor outputs. It should override `fuser_forward` instead of `op_forward`.
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Changes

- `transformer_engine/pytorch/ops/op.py:724`, `:759` — `BasicOperation.fuser_forward` / `fuser_backward` guards.
- `transformer_engine/pytorch/ops/basic/add_extra_input.py:47`, `:55`.
- `transformer_engine/pytorch/ops/basic/make_extra_output.py:52`, `:60`.

One character each, nothing else touched.

# Checklist:

- [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)
- [x] The functionality is complete
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [ ] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [ ] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

No test, and I would rather say so than claim otherwise. Reaching these lines needs a built extension plus a custom `BasicOperation` subclass that declares extra tensor inputs or outputs and implements `op_forward` instead of `fuser_forward`, and nothing in the tree asserts on this text today. I have no GPU and no built extension here.

What I did run: `black 24.4.2 --line-length=100 --preview --enable-unstable-feature=string_processing`, the exact arguments from `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, reports all three files unchanged, and `pylint 3.3.1 --rcfile=pylintrc` rates `add_extra_input.py` and `make_extra_output.py` 10.00/10. On `op.py` pylint reports `E0611: No name 'common' in module 'transformer_engine'`, which is the unbuilt extension on this machine and not related to the change.

Confidence Score: 5/5

**[Low impact]** This PR appears safe to merge; it fixes the class names in existing error messages.

Summary

Fixes six `RuntimeError` messages so they show the operation’s class name instead of `{self.__class__.__name__}`. - Fusible-operation errors now name the operation class. Reviews (1) · Last reviewed commit: ["\[PyTorch\] Interpolate the class name in ..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/4f0588b922fd6eddb70547cdc4687ad5efae5c85) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_expert&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=code_reviews&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

Thanks for the run. The one red check is `te-ci/L0_pytorch_unittest--H100_1GPU`, and it does not come from this change. That same job is red on ten of the eleven most recently merged PRs, #3662 included, which landed a few hours ago, and it is red on #3655 as well. Every other variant here is green, A100 and B200 and both debug runs, and the uploaded log for the H100 job comes back as `<EMPTY LOG>` so there is nothing in it to act on from outside.

No test depends on these strings, for what it is worth. Searching the repo for `operation has` hits six source files and zero tests. The three outside this diff, `swiglu.py`, `activation.py` and `grouped_linear.py`, already carry the `f`, so the six here were the whole remainder.
